ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a Cartesian coordinate system, there exists an ideal boundary intersecting the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B, with \angle AOB = 30^{\circ}. In the upper-right region of the boundary, there is a uniform magnetic field directed outward perpendicular to the plane of the paper, and in the lower-left region of the boundary, there is a uniform electric field of magnitude E directed along the +y direction. A positively charged particle is released from rest at the origin O, accelerated by the electric field, and enters the magnetic field at point B with a velocity $v_0$. It then exits the magnetic field directly at point A, with the time taken to travel from B to A being $t_0$. The gravitational force on the particle is negligible.

1. What is the time $t_1$ for the particle to move from O to B?
2. What is the magnitude $B$ of the magnetic induction?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Figure description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, with the x-axis to the right and the y-axis upward; the dashed boundary slants downward to the right from point B on the y-axis and intersects the x-axis at point A. Black dots are drawn in the region above/to the right of the dashed line, indicating a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface outward; upward arrows are drawn in the region below/to the left of the dashed line, indicating a uniform electric field along the +y direction. The particle goes from O upward along the y-axis to B, then enters the magnetic field region and finally leaves from A. In the figure, the acute angle between the boundary and the x-axis is 30°. Reasoning: Let OB=h. In right triangle OAB, since the angle between boundary AB and the x-axis is 30°, tan30°=OB/OA=h/OA, so OA=√3 h. When the particle enters the magnetic field from B, its velocity is upward; it carries positive charge and the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward, so the Lorentz force q v×B points to the right. Therefore the center C of the circular motion is to the right of B. Take C=(R,h), the coordinates of point B are (0,h), and the coordinates of point A are (√3h,0). Because A is on the circular orbit, it satisfies (√3h-R)^2+h^2=R^2. Expanding gives 3h^2-2√3hR+R^2+h^2=R^2, so 4h^2=2√3hR, obtaining R=2h/√3. Radius CB points left, and radius CA=(√3h-R,-h)=(h/√3,-h). The direction of motion from B to A is clockwise, and the central angle is 240°=4π/3. Therefore t0=(4π/3)/(v0/R)=4πR/(3v0). Substituting R=2h/√3 gives h=3√3 v0 t0/(8π). In the electric field, the particle undergoes uniformly accelerated straight-line motion from rest, and when it reaches B its speed is v0 and its displacement is h; therefore the average speed is v0/2, h=v0 t1/2. Thus t1=2h/v0=3√3 t0/(4π). Also, in the electric field stage qE t1/m=v0, that is m/q=E t1/v0; in the magnetic field stage the angular speed qB/m=(4π/3)/t0. So B=(m/q)·4π/(3t0)=(E t1/v0)·4π/(3t0)=√3 E/v0.
